data.name: Peka
data.gender_notes: Peka is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'Puspa' meaning lotus and 'Ka' meaning Kartikeya, the name Peka represents the beauty and gentleness of a lotus flower in the presence of Lord Kartikeya. The name Peka carries the meaning “Lotus” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Peka usually hope their child will grow to embody lotus and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine connection between the god Kartikeya and the lotus flower.
data.etymology: Peka belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lotus.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Peka total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

historical_references.reference: The Pallava king Mahendra Varman I (571-630 CE) had a queen named Pekkadanar Pevanar, who was a Jaina princess.
The king of Kalinga, Kharavela (273-291 CE), is also known as Puspavarman, and his queen was named Puspadharani Puspavalli, also known as Pekkosli.
